# Issue #7: touching intervals are not merged

`merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)])` returns `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]` but the documented
behaviour is that closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge into `[(1, 5)]`.
Unsorted input must also be handled. Fix `ranges/merge.py`.

content: All cases behave correctly: touching intervals merge, unsorted input is handled, and edge cases (empty list, single point) work.

arguments.summary: Fixed `ranges/merge.py` to resolve issue #7: the function now sorts the full input before merging (previously it assumed sorted input and only processed `intervals[1:]` against an unsorted first element), and the merge condition was changed from `start < last_end` to `start <= last_end` so that closed intervals sharing an endpoint (e.g. `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]`) merge into `[(1, 5)]`. Verified with the test suite (2 tests pass) and manual checks for unsorted, touching, empty, and single-point inputs.
